_meta.what_this_is: The classic kidney-stone treatment study (Charig et al. 1986), the textbook example of Simpson's paradox. Two treatments, A and B, each scored on small stones and large stones as (successes, cases). Treatment A has the higher success rate on small stones AND on large stones, yet a lower overall rate -- because A was used on far more of the hard (large-stone) cases, which have lower success for everyone. The confounder is stone size, unevenly distributed between the treatments.
_meta.counts_are: The published study counts, used as a fixture. The same segmentation applies to any A/B rate with an uneven confounder -- model-vs-model on easy/hard prompts, agent-vs-agent on simple/complex tasks.
